resources.string: Files are encrypted with AES-256 and authenticated with HMAC-SHA256, so tampering or corruption is always detected. Download the recovery kit below to encrypt or decrypt files from the command line - no app install needed. It works on macOS, Linux, Windows (via WSL or Git Bash), and Android terminal environments. Full setup and usage instructions are included as README.txt inside the download.

A zip file containing the recovery script and full instructions. After downloading, unzip it and read README.txt first before running the script. Requires OpenSSL 3.0+ - save the kit somewhere safe, independent of the app.
Download the recovery kit and save it somewhere safe - a cloud drive, a USB stick, wherever you won\'t lose it - so you can use it if the app becomes unavailable in the future.
This kit lets you encrypt or decrypt AESLocker files from the command line, without the app installed. It contains two files: aeslocker_recover.sh (the script) and this README.

Every command in this guide must be typed into a terminal (also called a command line or shell), not double-clicked. On macOS or Linux, open the app named Terminal. On Windows, use WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux) or Git Bash instead - Command Prompt and PowerShell will not run these commands. Each command below is shown on its own line, starting with a $ sign - type everything after the $ (not the $ itself).

"You need OpenSSL 3.0 or newer installed. To check your OpenSSL version, execute the following command in the terminal:

 $ %1$s

On macOS, the built-in 'openssl' is not real OpenSSL and will not work. To install a working copy, execute the following command in the terminal:

 $ %2$s"

"Before you can run the script for the first time, your system needs permission to execute it. In the folder where you extracted this kit, execute the following command in the terminal:

 $ %1$s

You only need to do this once."
"To encrypt a file, execute the following command in the terminal:\n\n $ %1$s"
"To decrypt a file, execute the following command in the terminal:\n\n $ %1$s"

You will be asked to type your password directly into the terminal. It is never shown on screen or saved anywhere. If you forget your password, this script cannot recover it for you - there is no way around this, by design.

"Linux users: most current distributions already include a compatible OpenSSL. To check your OpenSSL version, execute the following command in the terminal:

 $ %1$s

If you get an 'xxd: command not found' error when running the script, install it using your package manager - for example, on Debian or Ubuntu:

 $ %2$s"

"Android users: this script can run inside a terminal app such as Termux. Install Termux from F-Droid (the Google Play Store version is outdated and no longer maintained), open it, then install the required tools by executing the following command in the terminal:\n\n $ %1$s"

"Windows users: run this script (aeslocker_recover.sh) inside WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux) or Git Bash. It will not run in Command Prompt or PowerShell directly. Git Bash includes everything this script needs. WSL runs a real Linux distribution, so if you get an \'xxd: command not found\' error there, install it the same way as a Linux user would - for example, on Debian or Ubuntu:\n\n $ %1$s"
